cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1:1-2). He's just told them they aren't children of the slave woman but of the free woman (Galatians 4:31). Now he says it plain: "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free."

cards.question: Christ has set them free. So what does Paul tell the Galatians to do now?

answers.text: Work hard to earn their freedom

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that now they're free, the Galatians could never be weighed down by a yoke of slavery again.

cards.text: Go BACK to slavery? Friend, I did years in a junk drawer, and if that drawer opens and somebody says "come on back in," I am hopping the OTHER way, base and all. Now Paul signs his own name to a warning about circumcision: "Take notice: I, Paul, tell you..."

cards.question: If the Galatians let themselves be circumcised, what does Paul say Christ will be worth to them?
True or false: Paul says a man who gets himself circumcised is obligated to obey just that one command and nothing more.

cards.text: Then Paul speaks to anyone trying to be justified by the law. That reminds me of me when my edges went blurry, pressing HARDER and HARDER on the dough like harder was gonna fix it. Spoiler: it did not.

cards.question: What does Paul say about people who are trying to be justified by the law?

answers.text: They have been severed from Christ
They have drawn closer to Christ

cards.text: Then Paul tells how he and the believers wait for the hope of righteousness. They wait eagerly, through the Spirit.

cards.question: Paul says, "But by ___ we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness."
In Christ Jesus, Paul says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. So what does matter?

answers.text: Coming from the right family line

cards.text: Paul writes, "You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?" Friend, that's me on my first jog: cruising, FLYING, feeling GREAT, and then somebody steps in the way and I'm face down in the grass asking what year it is.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the persuasion that's slowing the Galatians down comes from the One who calls them.

cards.text: And then Paul pulls a picture straight out of MY kitchen. Leaven, friend. Dough! I have waited this ENTIRE letter for somebody to talk dough.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through how much of the dough?
Paul is confident in the Lord that the Galatians will take no other view. What does he say about the one troubling them, whoever he may be?

answers.text: He will be let off free
He will be put in charge

cards.text: Then Paul asks the brothers something. If he's still preaching circumcision, why is he still being persecuted?

cards.question: If Paul were still preaching circumcision, he says, "In that case the offense of the ___ has been abolished."

cards.text: Then Paul gets blunt about the people agitating the Galatians. He says he wishes they would go ahead and emasculate themselves.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers they were called to freedom. True or false: he says they should use that freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, "serve one another in love." Free to serve. That's the whole recipe, friend.

cards.question: Paul says the entire law is fulfilled in a single decree. Which one?
Paul warns that if the Galatians keep on biting and devouring one another, they will be ___ by one another.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "come on back in", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "But by ___ we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "In that case the offense of the ___ has been abolished.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card gives the free woman context from Galatians 4:31 but never says what is going on in Galatia: someone is pushing the believers toward circumcision and the law. Circumcision then appears out of nowhere on card 4, and the baker can't tell what the 'yoke of slavery' refers to.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Go BACK to slavery?', the junk drawer joke, and 'Now Paul signs his own name...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup calls Paul's next line 'a warning about circumcision'. That rules out the wrong answers on card 5 ('Even more value', 'The same value'), so only 'No value at all' fits a warning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin was 'pressing HARDER and HARDER on the dough' when his edges went blurry. In the backstory, Mother Miller pressed harder. Papa Dorin didn't. This changes his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Paul speaks...', 'That reminds me...' and 'Spoiler: it did not.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke says trying harder by the law-like effort 'did not' work. That tips the baker off before card 8 and rules out the wrong answers 'They have drawn closer to Christ' and 'They have earned extra grace'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card tells the second half of Galatians 5:4, 'you have fallen away from grace'. This is a key detail of the passage, and the baker never sees it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a jog through grass where Papa Dorin ends up face down. That is a new event in his world, outside his bakery. It also sits badly with a stamper who always moves on his gold base.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: 'And then Paul pulls a picture...', 'Leaven, friend.', 'Dough!' and 'I have waited...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording 'cross'. Nothing earlier sets up the cross, and card 6 gives no context to reason from. 'law' and 'temple' can only be ruled out by already knowing the verse.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Instead, Paul says...', 'Free to serve.' and 'That's the whole recipe, friend.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Calling serving one another in love 'the whole recipe' tells the baker, right before card 11, that love sums up everything. That rules out 'Remember the Sabbath day' and 'Honor your father and mother'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'rescued' and 'honored' aren't believable as the result of biting and devouring one another in a warning. Only 'consumed' makes sense.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.
